sections.h2: Which Palm Beach County office should I call about my tax bill?
sections.html:
It depends on the question. The Property Appraiser answers anything about value, exemptions and caps. The Tax Collector answers anything about the amount due and how to pay it. The Clerk and Comptroller runs the Value Adjustment Board and the tax deed auction.

The Tax Collector says it mails more than 600,000 property tax bills by November 1, and sends each to the address the appraiser has on file. If you moved or sold, correct the mailing address with the appraiser, not the collector.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, caps, the TRIM notice.
  • Tax Collector: bills, payment, installment plan, deferral, certificates.
  • Clerk and Comptroller: appeals board petitions and tax deed sales.

sections.h2: How big is Palm Beach County, and who lives in it?
sections.html:
The Census county page counts 1,575,726 people as of mid-2025. Its housing data for 2020 through 2024 gives owners a $447,300 midpoint home value and a 70.1 percent ownership rate, with household income at $83,581 in 2024 dollars. Those 65 or older are 26.1 percent of residents, so age-based relief touches a large share of bills.

The appraiser's municipality list shows how many cities and towns levy separately. Codes begin with 00 for unincorporated land and run through Atlantis, Belle Glade, Boca Raton, Boynton Beach, Delray Beach, Jupiter, Lake Worth Beach, Palm Beach, Pahokee, Tequesta, Wellington, West Palm Beach and Westlake. The first digits of a 17-digit parcel control number carry that code, so the number on your bill reveals which city taxes your lot.

sections.h2: What do the appraiser's exemption charts say for 2026?
sections.html:
They list more than a dozen exemptions, and a few have dollar limits that change yearly. The chart prints a 2026 household income limit of $38,686 in adjusted gross income for the senior exemption, and $37,712 in gross income for the civilian total and permanent disability and paraplegic or hemiplegic exemptions. Eligibility uses the prior year's income.

sections.h2: What do homestead filing and the caps require?
sections.html:
The appraiser asks for three things: title in your name, permanent Florida residence, and the home lived in on January 1. File by March 1, since a late filer loses that year's exemption. Online, service center and mail all work, and approval renews itself until something changes.

The first slice of $25,000 counts against every levy, schools included. A further slice of up to $25,000 starts once assessed value passes $50,000 and skips the school levy. Save Our Homes limits how far a homestead's assessment can rise in a year, using inflation or 3 percent, whichever is smaller; the state chart's 2026 entry is 2.7.

Property that is not homestead, such as a rental or second home, has a 10 percent cap on every levy except the school board's, and the appraiser notes the cap falls away the year after a sale. Report any change in ownership, marriage, divorce, death or use of the home to the appraiser.

sections.h2: When are Palm Beach County bills due, and how do discounts and installments work?
sections.html:
Payment opens November 1 and runs through March 31. Early payers save 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February; March carries the full amount.

April 1 starts delinquency. Per the collector, late tax is not payable online; funds must be in hand by the month's final working day to count, since a postmark stops mattering after delinquency.

The installment payment plan splits taxes into four payments due around June or July, September, December and March. The collector's 2026 deadline to apply was April 30, and enrollment for 2027 opens November 1, 2026. The collector's calendar for the current year controls the exact dates.

sections.h2: How does the tax work out when a Palm Beach County home sells?
sections.html:
An unpaid balance attaches to the parcel, so the closing table is where it ends. The title agent reads the bill and subtracts any payoff before paying the seller. Settle with the buyer how the current year's bill is split, because bills go out in November but closings occur in every month.

The deed carries state stamp tax at seventy cents per hundred dollars everywhere but Miami-Dade, and every signer answers to the state for it, whatever the contract assigns. Payment happens at the recording counter, next to the page fees set by section 28.24.

For the buyer, assessed value resets to market value from the next January 1. The seller's capped savings do not transfer, which is why a long-time neighbor's bill can differ sharply from a new owner's.

sections.h2: What happens if Palm Beach County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquency moves through fixed stages, and paying at any point before the auction ends it. The collector must hold an annual certificate sale no earlier than 60 days after delinquency or June 1, whichever is later. A certificate is a first lien bought by an investor who pays your tax in exchange for a competitive bid rate.

To redeem, you pay the delinquent tax, interest, advertising costs and a $6.25 collection fee added to each certificate. Certificates that draw no bidder go to the county, where the collector states interest runs at 18 percent annually.

After two years from delinquency, the certificate holder may file a tax deed application, and the clerk's office runs the sale. Redemption stays open until the sale itself. An owner behind on tax can still sell, because closing pays the balance.

sections.h2: What is the route for disputing a Palm Beach County assessment?
sections.html:
Phone the appraiser first. If the disagreement survives, file with the Value Adjustment Board. The appraiser's FAQ encourages that first call, and its records are searchable online.

On the appraiser's calendar, mid-September closes the window for market value appeals and denied portability claims, and a denied exemption has until July 31 or the 30th day after the denial notice. The state taxpayer page separately gives a 25-day limit counted from the TRIM mailing. Your own notice is the final word on timing. The Clerk runs the board independently of the appraiser, so ask for the current filing fee before you file.

faqs.q: Where does my Palm Beach County tax payment go?
faqs.a: To the Tax Collector, which bills and collects. The Property Appraiser only sets value and exemptions.

faqs.q: Does paying early cut a Palm Beach County bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The collector's schedule starts at 4 percent for November and falls a point monthly, ending after February.

faqs.q: Does homestead end when a Palm Beach County home is sold?
faqs.a: The sale ends it for that house. Apply again for your next home, and use portability to bring part of your capped savings along if you buy within three years.

faqs.q: What is the Super Senior exemption?
faqs.a: It exempts a qualifying owner from city levies in Boynton Beach or Delray Beach only. It needs 25 years of ownership and a market value under $250,000 at application.

faqs.q: Which office records a Palm Beach County deed?
faqs.a: The Clerk and Comptroller records it and collects the documentary stamp tax at that time.
